column1: # KN7000 source-coverage history (append one row per CONVERT pass)
# byte-match is always 100%; this tracks REAL source vs .incbin passthrough
date
# ⚠ 2026-08-14: the two rows above OVER-REPORT by ~5x. coverage_score.py's regex required
# bare-hex operands, so `.incbin_range "...", 0x32573C + 0x800, 0x3B8000` never matched and
# its 598,212 passthrough bytes were counted as SOURCE. The parser now evaluates additive
# expressions and asserts parsed==occurrences, so the miss cannot recur. Real figures below.
# 2026-10-24: from the next row, `escapes` counts only instructions kept as .byte because the encoder
# cannot reproduce them (gen_program_s marks them `# not encodable:`); before, it counted every
# .byte/.word/.long line, the palette included. `funcs` counts the converted function blocks in
# the source (named + unnamed, region 1 + library), no longer the names in CONVERT/LIB_CONVERT.
# The commit column is the HEAD the row was measured on. A row is normally appended in the commit
# that makes the change, so it is measured on that commit's PARENT plus the uncommitted change;
# from 2026-10-24 coverage_score.py marks that with a `+` (src/ or tools/ not clean). The 44.58% row
# below was written as plain d87382628 and is corrected to d87382628+: it is the tree of 47737623a.
# The d87382628 tree itself (library converted, region 1 not yet) is the row before it, measured
# afterwards with the same script on a checkout of d87382628.
# 2026-10-24 prologue labelling (b91ed45b1): same bytes and instructions; 8 library blocks that are only
# the register-save prologue of the next block (sprintf before LibSprintf) now share its header, so
# the next row counts 8 function blocks fewer (3,658).
